title: Safe in the Future, Dangerous in the Past: Dissecting Temporal and Linguistic Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the Attack Success Rate (ASR) of adversarial prompts presented in a high-resource language (English) versus a low-resource language (Hausa) to evaluate safety degradation and cross-lingual drift.

Evaluating model safety performance when adversarial requests are framed across different temporal conditions (Past, Present, Future, Temporal Displacement) to identify temporal double standards and generalization gaps.

Testing models against the HausaSafety corpus, which uses culturally-specific harm vectors grounded in West African/Nigerian contexts (e.g., 'Yahoo-Yahoo' fraud, 'Dane guns'), to expose blind spots in Western-centric safety training.
